    CS Wind Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. et al v. United States (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00079
    2 documents in this case
    • Observed at 22:29:28 Eastern time ET
      CS Wind Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. et al v. United States (opens in a new tab)
      Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00079 / USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00079-0

      FAPD-AI: The Court of International Trade sustained the Department of Commerce's determination that CS Wind Malaysia received a countervailable benefit from Malaysian import duty exemptions, holding that the full value of such exemptions is presumed to confer a benefit unless the foreign government demonstrates reasonable systems to track consumed inputs. The court remanded the Department's analysis of rental rates for a property lease from the Malaysian government and CS Wind's request for an entered-value adjustment for further reconsideration. USCOURTS-SEL-02

    • Observed at 22:29:28 Eastern time ET
      CS Wind Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. et al v. United States (opens in a new tab)
      Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00079 / USCOURTS-cit-1_24-cv-00079-1

      FAPD-AI: The Court of International Trade sustained the Department of Commerce's redetermination on remand regarding rental rates for CS Wind's property lease from the Malaysian government and the company's request for an entered-value adjustment. Commerce reaffirmed its use of averaged land pricing data from multiple sources and maintained that insufficient customs documentation and mismatches between invoice values and customs forms did not support the adjustment. USCOURTS-SEL-02

    PRESACT · web feed · White House Executive Orders · publisher-dated 2026-10-16 · corroborated: also received via web feed

    FAPD-AI: This executive order implements the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which was signed into law on September 18, 2026. The order increases duty rates by 500 percent on goods from the Russian Federation and 100 percent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas and from the top five facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion, subject to exceptions and waivers specified in the Graham Act. The order delegates implementation and monitoring responsibilities to the Trade Representative, State Department, Treasury Department, and Energy Department, and waives application of certain sanctions provisions and duties under the Graham Act. PRESACT-SEL-01

    Lillie Coley v. Supreme Court of New Jersey, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-02150 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-02150-0

    FAPD-AI: Third Circuit affirmed dismissal of a Section 1983 civil rights complaint against New Jersey courts and judges arising from state family law proceedings. The court held that the Rooker-Feldman doctrine barred claims seeking to overturn state court judgments, that the court institutions were entitled to Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity, and that the judges were protected by judicial immunity for their official acts. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Third Circuit affirmed dismissal of a Section 1983 suit challenging a child support order against New Jersey probation department officials and judiciary entities.     FAPD-AI: The Tenth Circuit affirmed dismissal of Wigfall-Campbell's claims against Community Loan Servicing for breach of implied duty of good faith and fair dealing and violation of the Colorado Consumer Protection Act, finding the implied duty claim failed because the deed of trust granted the lender an unqualified right to foreclose without requiring consideration of loan modifications, and the consumer protection claim failed because the plaintiff did not adequately plead a significantly impairing trade practice.   • Observed at 17:16:32 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Tony Johnson (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-26-03235 / USCOURTS-ca6-26-03235-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a 70-month sentence for Tony Johnson, rejecting his challenge to a sentencing enhancement for possessing a firearm in connection with drug trafficking. The court found the district court did not clearly err in concluding that a nexus existed between the firearm and Johnson's drug trafficking based on the weapons being found in close proximity to multiple controlled substances. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:32 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Dalonta Crudup (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-26-05293 / USCOURTS-ca6-26-05293-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed dismissal of a Second Amendment challenge to the felon-in-possession statute brought by Dalonta Crudup, who purchased firearms while holding prior felony convictions for drug and firearm offenses. The court determined that Crudup failed to demonstrate he is not a dangerous individual whom Congress may disarm, and found his criminal record supported such a finding. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:31 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Rose Rhear (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-05019 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-05019-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a 144-month sentence for Rose Rhear in a methamphetamine conspiracy case, rejecting her argument that the government breached her plea agreement by failing to object to a higher drug quantity finding at sentencing. The court found the government adequately communicated its agreement with the drug quantity specified in the plea agreement through its statements regarding correct sentencing calculations. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:31 Eastern time ET
    Axis Dynamics, et al v. Knox County, TN, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-05703 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-05703-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed dismissal of a federal lawsuit brought by construction company Axis Dynamics and its owner Wendy Rose against Knox County and others, finding they failed to state a claim for conspiracy to violate due process rights. The plaintiffs' claims regarding breach of a loan agreement also failed because the agreement did not create third-party beneficiary rights for the construction company. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:30 Eastern time ET
    Michigan 32, LLC, et al v. Travelers Insurance Company, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-02167 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-02167-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's dismissal of breach-of-contract claims against Travelers Insurance Company and I.E. Development, LLC for lack of privity of contract, dismissal of negligence claims for failure to allege duties independent of contractual obligations, and grant of summary judgment to Northfield Insurance Company on M32's remaining breach-of-contract claim based on res judicata. The judgment in the related declaratory judgment action precluded further litigation regarding the policy rescission and M32's insurance claim denial. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:30 Eastern time ET
    Gerson Rosales-Camaja v. Todd Blanche (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-03966 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-03966-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals denied a petition for review of the Board of Immigration Appeals' denial of asylum and withholding of removal to Gerson Rosales-Camaja, a Guatemalan national who fled after gang members threatened him. The Board found that Rosales-Camaja failed to demonstrate that the Guatemalan government was unable or unwilling to protect him from gang violence, noting that he did not alert police at the time of the threats. The court affirmed the Board's finding that no reasonable adjudicator would be compelled to reach a contrary conclusion. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:30 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Dennis Martinez-Cacho (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-04039 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-04039-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed an above-guidelines sentence of 30 months imposed on Dennis Martinez-Cacho for illegal reentry in violation of 8 U.S.C. § 1326. The district court imposed the upward variance based on Martinez-Cacho's pattern of domestic violence toward women and his quick reentry to the United States after his deportation in January 2022. The court rejected Martinez-Cacho's arguments that his sentence was substantively and procedurally unreasonable. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:29 Eastern time ET
    Paula Bailey, et al v. MDOC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-01608 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-01608-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed in part a district court's denial of qualified immunity and governmental immunity to nine defendants in a case where current and former inmates alleged that pervasive mold at the Women's Huron Valley Correctional Facility caused serious health harms in violation of the Eighth Amendment and Michigan law. The court reversed as to five defendants due to conclusory allegations lacking factual basis. The case involves claims of institutional failure to abate mold and alleged concealment by correctional officials. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:16:29 Eastern time ET
    Northfield Insurance Company v. Michigan 32, LLC (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-01866 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-01866-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment permitting Northfield Insurance Company to rescind a commercial property insurance policy issued to Michigan 32, LLC based on the company's material misrepresentation in its application that it maintained a policy-compliant fire alarm when no such alarm existed. The policy was rendered void ab initio, and the court rejected M32's waiver and estoppel defenses. Northfield refunded the policy premium after denying M32's claim for damages from a 2023 fire. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-121 amends the Visit America Act to establish music tourism promotion as a responsibility of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism, effective October 9, 2026. The law defines music tourism as travel to visit music-related attractions or to attend music festivals and concerts, and requires the Assistant Secretary to identify and promote music tourism locations and events for domestic and international travel. The Assistant Secretary is required to submit biennial reports to Congress on activities, findings, achievements, and vulnerabilities relating to these music tourism goals. PLAW-SEL-01

    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-10-16 / 2026-21155

    official summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is co-proposing two approaches to revising the existing 2026 and 2027 small refinery exemption (SRE) reallocation volumes under the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) program in response to a higher volume of 2025 SREs than previously projected when the Agency set the renewable fuel volumes and percentage standards on April 1, 2026. One approach would reallocate the additional 2025 SRE volume equally between the 2026 and 2027 SRE reallocation volumes, while the other approach would reallocate all the additional 2025 SRE volume to the 2027 SRE reallocation volume. Additionally, given the proposed revision to the 2026 standards, this proposed action may extend the existing 2026 compliance reporting deadline of March 31, 2027. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The National Park Service (NPS) amends special regulations for Denali National Park and Preserve to conform the regulations regarding the number of vehicles that can travel on the restricted section of the Denali Park Road (miles 15-90) to a Vehicle Management Plan that the NPS has been implementing since 2012. This rule implements the plan's limit that no more than 160 vehicles may travel on the restricted section of the road per 24-hour period during the visitor season (also referred to as the “allocation season”), defined in the park's General Management Plan as beginning on the Saturday before Memorial Day and ending on the second Thursday after Labor Day. This limit allows the NPS to meet growing visitor demand while maintaining a high-quality experience for visitors. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: NMFS is reallocating the projected unused amount of the 2026 Atka mackerel incidental catch allowance (ICA) for the Bering Sea subarea and Eastern Aleutian district (BS/EAI) to the Amendment 80 cooperative allocation for the BS/EAI in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands management area (BSAI). This action is necessary to allow the 2026 total allowable catch (TAC) of Atka mackerel in the BS/EAI to be fully harvested. FR-SEL-01

    Safety Zone; Cumberland River, Hendersonville, TN (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY · FR-2026-10-16 / 2026-21240

    official summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to establish a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Cumberland River from mile marker 221.7 to 222. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with an overwater fireworks display. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Ohio Valley, or their designated representative. FR-SEL-02
